DESIGN SPEC:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ONE finished independent single flat opaque poster, portrait width:height 2:3. Create only the assigned R7-D1-M3 image; the five ratios above describe the common series, not five outputs for this call.
요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력

Design: Two connected parts work together while turning at different rates. Make a decisive constructed cut-paper graphic of exactly two unequal, mechanically credible spur gears, face-on, in one plane. The large gear occupies the lower-left field, the smaller gear the upper-right field. The line between their centers rises diagonally across the page. Their teeth MUST interlock visibly at the shared diagonal contact: equal tooth pitch and matching tooth size, alternate tooth into valley, no overlapping solid tooth tips, no unexplained gap, no gear sitting on top of the other. The large wheel has roughly twice the pitch diameter and twice as many teeth as the small wheel. Resolve their proportion and contact carefully. The two substantial wheel bodies and working mesh must remain recognizable at thumbnail size even if the title is hidden. Preserve the entire meshing contact inside the frame and leave all text clear of it.

Composition: A large deep cobalt-blue toothed cut-paper wheel rises from the lower-left, and a smaller vermilion-orange toothed cut-paper wheel sits above and to the right. Keep generous but purposeful pale warm-gray paper around the outer silhouettes. Neither wheel is an isolated decorative disk. Both have small plain round central hubs, no labels or marks. Their centers, unequal radii and shared teeth organize the entire composition.

Motion: Inset a broad contrasting swept paper sector on each wheel, concentric to its hub, with clean radial ends. The small wheel's sector spans about twice the angle of the large wheel's sector. Orient the visible sweeps in opposite rotational senses. Use the sectors as subordinate angular displacement cues, not arrows, orbit lines or substitute mechanisms. Their shapes stay inside the circular wheel bodies and remain distinct from tooth silhouettes and from the letter strokes. No arrows, measurements, ticks, numerals or annotation.

Typography and placement: Place the only supplied title as a single compact, firm, dark Hangul block in the shared wedge of negative space adjacent to and just above-left of the mesh. Use three balanced horizontal lines, each a whole word in the original order. This is one occurrence of the title, soft wrapping between words; do not split any syllable, rotate the type or repeat the title. Use unwarped, naturally proportioned Korean sans-serif with substantial open counters and steady stroke weight. The title's block balances the small wheel across the gear contact; it is not a top header or a bottom caption. Maintain a deliberate open gap between title edges and teeth. The title must be readable at reduced size.

Material: Layered solid matte dyed paper with crisp, deliberate scissor-cut tooth silhouettes, restrained short contact shadows consistently down-right. The two wheels inhabit the same shallow layer and cast the same kind of shadow. Very subtle paper fiber only; do not fill all surfaces with coarse speckling. Give broad sectors their own thin paper-layer edge. Maintain coherent planes and sharp edges throughout. No glossy mechanical rendering, dimensional type, mockup, frame, panel, logos, watermarks, incidental text, extra symbols, confetti or ornamental filler.
